Naming traps verified in the package:

- NeuButtonComponent selects a native button with the neu-button attribute. Its domain output is neuClick.
- The /modal entrypoint exports NeuDialogComponent with selector neu-dialog. Never infer the exported name or selector from the entrypoint filename.
- The Angular FormField directive belongs to @angular/forms/signals. Neural's NeuFormFieldComponent is a layout shell and label/hint/error association API.

The root entrypoint intentionally does not re-export the whole component catalog. Entry points marked internal by the source policy are excluded even if package.json physically lists them. Generated declarations can reference private dependency types; that is not authorization to import those types from implementation files. Use only an exported type from an admitted public entrypoint.

The API catalog is a structural inventory. Runtime behavior, accessibility and state ownership still need the relevant reference and an integration check. It is not a certification of every component.

# Forms and Signal Forms

Neural v2 signal controls implement Angular's Signal Forms control contracts. They do not implement ControlValueAccessor. Do not attach ngModel, formControl or formControlName to them. An application can retain reactive forms elsewhere; do not force the old binding onto a Neural signal control.

Start from the compiled [forms.ts](../examples/forms.ts). It imports FormField, form, required and minLength from @angular/forms/signals and NeuInputComponent from /input. The application signal owns the data; form creates a stable field tree; [formField] connects the Neural control to the field.

Use one value owner for a control: FormField or its documented model binding. Never add [value]/valueChange on the same control already owned by FormField. The example's separate Select illustrates explicit model binding instead.

Keep the field tree stable. Declare it once, not in a getter or template expression. Apply validation through the schema. Distinguish invalid, pending, touched and dirty: an empty required control can be invalid before interaction. Choose application error text based on the actual field errors and the intended display policy. The sample's single text message is deliberately simple.

Reset through the field state API when interaction state must reset too. Merely replacing the model's data does not express the same reset. A reset required field remains invalid if its reset value is empty. In the sample, fields.name().reset('') resets both value and touched/dirty state.

For disabled and readonly behavior, check Angular's Signal Forms schema rules and the individual Neural control's inputs. Do not equate readonly with disabled or attach competing owners for the same state. Model value types vary: inspect [input](api/input.md), [checkbox](api/checkbox.md), [switch](api/switch.md), [select](api/select.md), [date-input](api/date-input.md) and [option-api](api/option-api.md) for the specific control. Never assume all controls expose value or the same nullability.

For Select, use typed optionLabel/optionValue accessors and an explicit mode. Single mode emits a scalar or null; multiple mode uses a readonly value array. Preserve the application's domain identity and compareWith rules when objects are used. Do not copy v1 optionLabel strings into function-based APIs without checking the current declaration.

For a custom native input in a Neural form shell, connect label and input IDs using NeuFormFieldComponent's forId and the native input id. The shell does not turn an arbitrary control into a Signal Forms control.

Sources: [Neural v2 Signal Forms](https://ui.neuralui.org/v2/en/foundations/signal-forms), [Angular Signal Forms](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/signals/overview).

# Layout and accessibility

Use semantic HTML and application CSS Grid/Flexbox for page composition. Neural Card, Panel, Splitter and DashboardGrid serve specific contracts; do not invent a universal Neural layout component. Inspect their individual API references before composing them.

Use public spacing, typography, surface and border tokens from [the catalog](api/tokens.md). Prefer logical CSS properties, min-width: 0 on flexible children, and explicit local overflow on wide data regions. Test narrow viewports with real data and long labels. Avoid hiding content merely to suppress document overflow.

Use an application-wide border-box sizing baseline for elements and pseudo-elements. The integration fixture applies this reset so control padding and borders stay within the available width. This is application CSS, not a private component override.

Every form control needs a meaningful accessible name. Prefer each control's documented label input or explicit label/ID associations. Keep labels distinct from placeholders. Connect hint and error text through the supported contracts. Preserve aria-invalid and required semantics, and inspect the resulting native control, not only the Angular host.

Use native buttons and links for their corresponding actions. Neural Button is button[neu-button]; give icon-only actions an ariaLabel and use an appropriate type in forms. Keep keyboard navigation, visible focus, disabled semantics and focus order intact.

For Tabs verify tablist/tab/tabpanel names, selected state and arrow-key behavior. For tables use meaningful column headers and stable row identity. For Dialog verify its name, Escape behavior, focus containment and restoration. Accepting or rejecting a close proposal must match the product's intended behavior.

Test zoom, reduced motion, forced colors, light/dark contrast, validation announcements and screen-reader behavior where required. The bundled Chromium checks cover specific naming, keyboard and focus scenarios plus a narrow layout; they are not a WCAG conformance certificate or an assistive-technology audit.

Use Angular CLI's SSR setup and preserve its browser/server entrypoints. Configure provideClientHydration with withEventReplay in the shared application providers. Neural does not enable Angular hydration itself. No production backend or hosting service is required to install this skill; SSR verification uses a temporary local test server.

Use the same initial data, IDs, selected tab, theme mode, locale, timeZone and clock decisions on server and client. Configure optional locale/timeZone/now through the root provideNeuralUI contract when relevant. Do not independently call the current time on both sides for visible initial content; transfer or otherwise reuse an application-owned timestamp.

The repository compiles the same example components into browser and server bundles, serves request-time SSR, checks HTML with JavaScript disabled, and then exercises hydrated interactions while rejecting browser errors. # State ownership, tables, navigation and overlays

Determine ownership from the real contract, never from a Change suffix alone.

| Contract | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | Application supplies a value | Button.disabled |
| Model | Component can edit the documented value | Input.value/valueChange |
| Proposal | Application accepts or rejects a request | Dialog.closeRequested |
| Domain event | Reports an action and its payload | Button.neuClick |
| Lifecycle | Reports an applied transition | Dialog.opened/closed |
| Derived internals | No consumer state ownership implied | Internal disabled activation guard |

## Tables

Use the compiled [table.ts](../examples/table.ts) and [table API](api/table.md). Provide a stable rowKey accessor returning domain keys; do not use row indices for mutable datasets. Supply readonly data and typed columns. The application owns query and selection. queryChange supplies the next query; selectionChange supplies an event whose next property is the proposed selection. Write each into the corresponding input signal. Never mutate rows, selection arrays or query objects in place.

The canonical query includes page (zero-based), pageSize, search, sort and filters. Do not revive fragmented v1 paging/sort inputs. Read the exported query and selection types before adding a feature; all-matching selection is a separate discriminated variant, not a list of loaded rows.

Remote mode is application-owned orchestration. Inspect NeuTableDataRequest and NeuTableMetadata: requestId, queryRevision and appliedRequestId describe which data belongs to which request. Preserve this provenance, ignore stale responses and update metadata consistently with applied data. Do not label the client-only example as a tested remote implementation. This repository adds no backend or network data source.

## Navigation

The compiled [navigation.ts](../examples/navigation.ts) uses controlled Tabs: activeId comes from one signal and activeIdChange proposes a tab ID or null. Keep tabId values aligned with tab IDs. An initialActiveId seed belongs to an uncontrolled setup; do not switch ownership mid-lifecycle. Check each other navigation component's own state contract; Tabs is not automatically a router. Angular Router owns application URLs and routes.

## Overlays

The compiled [overlays.ts](../examples/overlays.ts) uses /modal's NeuDialogComponent. Application open is an input. closeRequested carries a NeuCloseRequest and does not close the dialog until the application updates open. It can be rejected. Do not invent openChange or [(open)] for Dialog. opened and closed report applied lifecycle transitions, not permission to mutate state.

Keep an accessible title, keyboard dismissal, focus containment and return focus. Update the owner signal through the handler rather than imperatively manipulating the DOM. Public services and imperative methods are documented separately in [modal](api/modal.md), [popover](api/popover.md) and [foundation](api/foundation.md). Select's open/openChange pair is a different contract; do not copy Dialog event names into it. A global dismissal guard is synchronous and uses the public foundation provider if the application needs one.

Source: [official v2 state ownership](https://ui.neuralui.org/v2/en/foundations/state-ownership).

Load public global styles first; see [installation](installation.md). Defaults work without a preset. For customization use the compiled [theme.ts](../examples/theme.ts), [root configuration API](api/core.md) and [public token catalog](api/tokens.md).

defineNeuPreset from the root entrypoint defines a named, typed light/dark token map. Register that object via provideNeuralUI with theme.preset in the application's providers. The repository's integration app uses exactly that configuration. Missing tokens retain their mode defaults; a preset does not select the current mode.

The application selects the mode through data-theme="light" or data-theme="dark" on the document element. Use Angular's injected DOCUMENT and apply browser-only preference detection in a browser render phase. Keep server/browser initial mode identical; do not read localStorage or matchMedia at module scope. The example switches mode in response to a user action and starts consistently in light mode.

Use public token names from the generated catalog or NeuTokenName exported by foundation. Never invent a token, copy private component variables, or assume a v1 variable survives. CSS cannot type-check token names: this repository scans authored SCSS as well as compiling typed presets.

The preset example changes only a few tokens. For a production palette, review the complete foreground/background pairs, button-specific tokens, focus indicators, disabled states and contrast in every mode. A successful typed preset compilation is not a contrast audit.

Root data-neu-theme="high-contrast" and forced-colors handling take precedence over custom preset values. Preserve these behaviors, reduced motion and focus visibility. Do not force themes by replacing internal component styles.

For build-time CSS generation, neuPresetCss is available from [foundation](api/foundation.md); the ordinary application path is defineNeuPreset plus provideNeuralUI. Keep CSS configuration trusted; do not accept arbitrary untrusted CSS as a preset.

Source: [official v2 theming](https://ui.neuralui.org/v2/en/foundations/theming).

# Version maintenance

This installed skill is a snapshot for 2.0.3. Before applying it to another version, inspect the actual package exports, declarations and changelog; do not claim coverage for an untested release.

Maintainers regenerate API references from the installed npm tarball's declarations using the Neural AI repository's api:generate command. api:check compares exports, full declaration hashes, input/output aliases, domain declarations, public tokens and style hashes with the reviewed snapshot. Any change requires review; regeneration alone does not certify compatibility.

For a new release, maintainers update the exact package pin and lockfile, capture npm integrity and the matching source commit, review changes to the upstream support policy, regenerate, and run structural/import checks, negative tests, strict Angular builds and browser scenarios. Review the short authored references only where behavioral contracts changed. The generated API catalog does not require hand-editing every component.

Keep supported version metadata, examples and evidence consistent. Older versions are mentioned only in migration or historical evidence, never as active install targets. Keep Native imports excluded. Remove stale generated entrypoint files when an entrypoint disappears; do not retain an obsolete reference as a compatibility alias.

Agent specifications can change independently of Neural. Recheck [Codex skill locations](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills/), [Claude Code skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) and [Agent Skills format](https://agentskills.io/specification) when changing packaging. Portable frontmatter, relative references and complete directory copying avoid unnecessary per-agent forks.

After deterministic checks, run the separate agent evaluation prompts in the repository's tests/agent-scenarios.md with actual Codex and Claude Code sessions. Record agent versions, output, compilation and interaction results. Never mark these evaluations passed just because structural validation succeeded.
